topic: Car gas cap: why does it click when you tighten it? (torque-limiting ratchet: flexible arms on the cover drive inclined teeth on the cap body; once the seal is tight the arms bend, ride over the teeth and click, so the cap cannot be overtightened; loosening drives the steep faces with no slip).
principle: The handle you turn is not fixed to the part that seals: two flexible plastic arms on the handle press into inclined teeth on the cap body, so when tightening they drive the body only until the seal is tight; past that torque the arms bend outward, ride over each ramp and snap into the next tooth with a click, while turning the other way they push the steep tooth faces and the cap comes off without slipping.

firstComment:
Answer: two bendy plastic arms 🔧

The handle you turn isn't fixed to the part that seals. Inside, two flexible arms on the handle press into a ring of slanted teeth on the cap body.

Turn it to tighten: the arms push on the slopes and the whole cap turns, until the rubber seal is tight and the cap stops.

Keep turning: now the arms bend outward, ride up a slope and drop into the next tooth. Click! That's the torque limiter: you can't overtighten it and crush the seal, and the clicks tell you it's closed properly.

Turn it to loosen: the arms push on the steep side of the teeth, so they can't slip and the cap comes right off.

(Simplified 3D model, enlarged. Real caps vary: some have more arms, teeth on the other side, or a wavy spring.)

Sources:
US Patent 5,110,003, Torque-override cap (drive teeth on the shell engage inclined teeth on a ratchet wheel: torque-limited in the cap-advancing direction, positive in the cap-removal direction; overtightening can crush the O-ring gasket; extra torque gives a characteristic clicking noise): https://patents.justia.com/patent/5110003
US Patent 7,516,867, Cap device having torque mechanism (click units on the cover ride over projections when the torque exceeds a preset level; the click confirms the cap is fastened): https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/7516867
US 2006/0283860, Fuel filler cap (rotate the cap clockwise until a click sound is generated a few times): https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/20060283860
altText: 3D animation of a car gas cap. A black gas cap with a grip bar sits in the fuel filler pocket of a blue car body panel, under the question Why does it click? An orange arrow turns the cap clockwise. Then the cap's top and grip fade away to show the inside: a light gray ring of 12 slanted teeth on the cap body and two orange flexible arms on the handle, whose tips sit between the teeth. While tightening, the arms push the teeth and the whole cap turns until it stops on the seal. Turning further, each arm bends outward, rides up a slanted tooth and drops into the next one, click, three times. Then the arrow turns the other way: the arm tips push the steep side of the teeth and the cap turns back without slipping. The top fades back in and the video loops. Text on screen: Why does it click? Inside the cap. Sealed. It stops. The arm bends. Click! It skips. Can't overtighten it. Loosen: it grabs. Follow, new machine tomorrow.
